sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: On-Site Factory Pre-Shipment Quality Control and Audit Agency

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 710-1 to 710-27 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and company accounts, Article 5; Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions and the exercise of a commercial activity, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) together with coordinated articles of association, filed electronically by the notary via the LBR/RCS e-filing interface
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SARL minimum issued share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash before RCS registration; funds are held in a notary's blocked client account or a Luxembourg credit institution until registration. Simplified one-euro SARL (S.à r.l.-S) is not used in this dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company's share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 1,000 fully paid-up shares of EUR 12.00 each, is approved, subscribed, and paid up in cash, as confirmed by the notary's escrow certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted at 12, Rue de Strasbourg, L-2561 Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, where the central administration and statutory records shall be maintained. RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] are appointed managers (gérants), each acting individually, with authority to manage the business, open and operate bank accounts, sign agreements, and represent the company in its factory inspection, testing, quality-control, and audit agency operations. RESOLVED, that the managers are authorized to complete all Luxembourg Business Registers and administrative filing formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability check and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), central RCS unit — electronic name reservation portal at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online pre-registration request or instruct the appointed notary to conduct a name availability search and provisional reservation. The proposed name must be distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public order, and must include the mandatory legal form suffix 'S.à r.l.' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée'. The reservation is valid for two calendar months and will be extended only if RCS registration is initiated before expiry.
required_dossiers: copy of founder's passport or national ID card
draft articles of association showing the proposed company name
online name reservation form from LBR
short corporate purpose and business scope statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS office issues a name conflict or objection, submit a corrected second-choice name through the same portal or to the notary within five business days; meet any additional uniqueness evidence requested. A final rejection can be appealed to the Registrar under the relevant RCS procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of statutory corporate deed before Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg — notary admitted to practice in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear before the notary or be represented by a notarized power of attorney. The notary will read and verify the articles of association, confirm the legal capacity of the founders, record the share subscription, and physically execute the instrument of incorporation. The notarial deed must state the registered office, corporate object, share capital, number and nominal value of shares, management structure, and appointment of officers. The notary then prepares the certified RCS filing package.
required_dossiers: identity documents of each founder
duly signed articles of association in French, German, or English as accepted by the notary
notarized power of attorney for any absent founder
letters of consent of proposed managers
registered office address evidence: lease agreement, utility invoice, or domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects any irregularity in identity, signature, or consents, the parties must remedy the issue by signing a supplementary rectification instrument under the same notary, after which the deed is re-read and re-executed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and verification of statutory paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary's segregated client escrow account in a Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders transfer at least EUR 12,000 to the notary's escrow account in the company's name. The notary obtains written bank confirmation stating the amount, account name, and absence of encumbrance. The confirmation is attached to the notarial deed. If in-kind contributions are used, a statutory auditor's valuation report must be deposited and summarised in the deed. The capital cannot be returned or borrowed back before registration.
required_dossiers: bank credit confirmation or swift transfer evidence
notary's capital receipt certificate
in-kind contribution valuation report, if any
declaration of subscription by all founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank confirmation is ambiguous or not credited, instruct the bank to issue a corrected certificate or return the remittance and re-transmit, ensuring the booking date precedes the notarial deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-filing interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the notarial deed and required attachments electronically using the LBR e-filing interface. The system validates the file number, legal form, and capacity. The RCS assigns a corporate registration number and status 'registered'. The company acquires legal personality upon registration. Subsequent public publication is automatic via the electronic RCS; no physical gazette proof is required.
required_dossiers: executed notarial deed of incorporation
coordinated articles of association
LBR/RCS standard registration data sheet
capital deposit certificate from notary
written acceptances and consents of managers
specimen signatures of managers
domiciliation agreement if registered office is provided by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files a modification request, the notary submits a corrective filing through the same portal within the legal time limit. If the registration is refused, lodge a rectified deed and request prioritisation; appeal to the Registrar if a deficient notice is not cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration corporate activation and governance start-up
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Common Social Security Centre (CCSS), and Ministry of the Economy for licensing track
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the RCS extract, the company must file its employer registration with the CCSS to obtain the Luxembourg social security number, open a corporate bank account, adopt the first board minutes, and appoint any tax representatives. The managers must hold the inaugural board meeting, approve bank signatory cards, authorise expenditures, and implement internal accounting procedures. The business licence application under the Law of 2 September 2011 must be lodged in parallel with the Ministry of the Economy before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate or extract
board resolution appointing bank signatories
directors' passports and residence permits
completed CCSS employer registration form
business plan and liability insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CCSS or the Ministry requests amendments, align the corporate deed with the application and resubmit; if RCS data mismatch appears, obtain an updated RCS extract and send it to all authorities within five business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy — Directorate for the Authorization of Establishments and the Exercise of Commercial Activities (autorisation d'établissement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (State establishment licence) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions and the exercise of a commercial activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Agency) under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 'non soumis' / exempt from full environmental impact assessment for pure inspection, testing, and audit field services; a simple municipal zoning and registration confirmation is sufficient. If an in-house laboratory is established for destructive testing using solvents or chemical reagents, the activity is treated as a light service installation subject to prior notification only.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial process wastewater; sanitary wastewater discharged in accordance with municipal sewerage ordinance. No significant volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions; any solvent usage shall remain below EU solvent-emission ceilings, with adequate exhaust ventilation if engine or calibration equipment is operated. Hazardous sample residues, batteries, and chemical waste must be collected by an authorised waste operator in accordance with the Luxembourg waste management plan and the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; manifests must be retained at the registered office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) confirming exit routes, fire extinguishers, and smoke alarms; communal building occupancy permit for the registered office and any testing rooms; structural load clearance from a registered civil engineer for any stationary testing equipment over 500 kg; workplace health and safety inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) before personnel are deployed; public and professional liability insurance covering factory inspection errors and omissions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Luxembourg; e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu); professional e-filing via AEDT eSpace/eTVA; business register: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities first obtain an LBR business registration number (RCS number) via the RCS filing through MyGuichet.lu; after incorporation (or for a non-established deemed taxable person), file VAT registration Form No. 102 ('Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA') with the AEDT, annexing articles of association, certificate of incorporation, proof of place of business, list of directors/managers, description of taxable activities and anticipated turnover, and, for third-country entities, designation of an approved tax representative ('représentant responsable solidaire') established in Luxembourg; a Luxembourg VAT number (LU + 8 digits) is then issued within 2-4 weeks; a non-established EU supplier may use simplified registration where no local establishment exists but must register before any taxable transaction if VAT is chargeable in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Luxembourg SARL is an entity-level taxpayer (no pass-through election; aggregate Luxembourg City rate 24.94% comprising 17% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax). No US-style check-the-box election exists. Available elections and regimes: (1) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for Luxembourg-resident group companies upon prior AEDT approval; (2) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) with prior authorization, allowing one VAT ID for intra-group supplies; (3) participation-exemption election exercised via the annual CIT return for qualifying dividend and capital-gains exemption; (4) notional interest deduction (also known as VIVCES deduction) election; (5) advance tax agreements (APA) and tax ruling applications to determine hybrid mismatch treatment; ATAD hybrid-mismatch and CFC rules are mandatory with no opt-out.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA / Mehrwertsteuer – MwSt.)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-enterprise VAT franchise regime, Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law). A Luxembourg-established entity may apply the exemption below this threshold, but a SARL conducting cross-border inspections must register if it makes intra-Community acquisitions above EUR 10,000 or any taxable supplies to non-business customers; non-established foreign businesses have no threshold and must register before carrying out taxable transactions in Luxembourg (B2B supplies to a Luxembourg taxable customer are reverse-charged).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing: public authorities must receive structured e-invoices (EN 16931 / PEPPOL BIS 3.0) via a certified PEPPOL access point from 1 June 2023; suppliers under State/public-sector contracts are obliged to issue e-invoices from 1 January 2024 (or in tenders where e-invoicing is explicitly required). No real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls (CTC), no SAF-T filing, no digital stamp and no pre-clearance API apply in Luxembourg; B2B and B2C invoicing remain paper/PDF-permitted subject to authenticity and integrity archival rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to goods physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by or on behalf of the supplier; the chargeable event starts the 90-day proof-of-export period (extendable to one year in justified cases). On-site factory pre-shipment QC services physically performed outside Luxembourg (non-EU location) fall outside Luxembourg place-of-supply rules and are not chargeable to Luxembourg VAT; B2B inspection/testing services rendered from Luxembourg to an EU business customer are reverse-charged in the customer's member state (no Luxembourg VAT). Zero-rating mainly covers physical export of equipment, samples and goods re-delivered after testing, supported by transport and customs evidence, while services to non-EU customers must be evidenced by commercial contracts, inspection/test certificates and the customer's foreign TIN/VAT identification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT payment receipt
Commercial invoice and export packing list
Evidence of physical exit from the EU (customs stamp, ICS/ECS status messages, port/airport loading documents)
Laboratory test certificate or inspection report evidencing the service scope
Declaration by the foreign customer with respective TIN/VAT ID
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT audits export zero-rating strictly on documentary chain integrity; post-export adjustments and retrospective clawbacks reclassify the supply to Luxembourg VAT at 17% where proof of export is not obtained within 90 days, with automatic 0.8% monthly late interest (10% per annum), omission penalties of 10%-20% of the tax, and bad-faith surcharges up to 100% of the evaded tax; willful fraud attracts criminal fines (EUR 750-12,500) and imprisonment up to 5 years; abusive claims of export status in hybrid arrangements additionally trigger ATAD/GAAR economic-substance review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking prudential supervision; the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance retains general financial policy oversight. The BCL implements European Central Bank (ECB) monetary policy and manages euro system liquidity for Luxembourg-resident entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full participant in the European Economic and Monetary Union and the eurozone single currency area. There are no exchange control laws, no foreign exchange licensing requirements, and no restrictions on the conversion or repatriation of capital for current account or capital account transactions. Transaction convertibility is total for both residents and non-resident owners, subject only to general anti-money laundering, sanctions screening, EU/UN sanctions compliance, and Luxembourg company law solvency requirements. Profit remittance is unrestricted, but dividends paid by an SARL are subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at 15% unless reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, an applicable double tax treaty, or the participation exemption regime. No central bank approval or exchange control declaration is required for wire transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, no minimum conversion ratio, and no mandatory repatriation of export receivable proceeds into euro. Because ISIC 7120 inspection and testing services are exported services rather than physical goods, invoices may be settled in any agreed convertible currency. If foreign currency receipts are credited to a Luxembourg bank account, they may be held, converted, or remitted freely. However, for prudential risk management and treasury efficiency, it is recommended that all non-euro export receipts be converted to euro within bankable business day settlement cycles or hedged to eliminate translation exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / High-Value Client Treasury Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise (Wisdomtree Financial Europe, authorised as an electronic money institution in Belgium with EU passporting rights under the E-Money Directive) can be used for low-value cross-border disbursements and vendor payments in a compatible auxiliary role. Feasibility rating is Medium-High for ancillary payment rails; however, it is not a full substitute for a regulated credit institution in Luxembourg. For capital escrow, statutory audit evidence, and large outbound trade settlements, a licensed Luxembourg credit institution is mandatory. The CSSF does not recognise Wise as a domestic depositary bank, and funds held with such EMIs are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee scheme except through the home state scheme under EU law. Legal constraint: treasury policy should cap EMI balances and require immediate daily sweeps to a tier-1 Luxembourg bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an SARL with non-resident directors, the large majority of Luxembourg banks will require at least one board member or authorised signatory with legal capacity to attend an in-person or video-identification KYC interview. True fully remote opening is permitted for low-risk corporate clients only where the bank applies a secure video-identification process and CSSF-compliant remote onboarding standards. In practice, the final account opening decision rests with the bank's AML/KYC committee. For this ISIC 7120 standard-risk inspection agency, one physical meeting in Luxembourg with the ultimate beneficial owner and the statutory manager is strongly advisable to avoid rejection, although the bank may accept a remote interview accompanied by notarised corporate documents apostilled under the Hague Convention.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained beneficial ownership chain involving non-EU corporate shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain of ownership from the SARL to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner, certified share register, notarised shareholder resolutions, apostilled certificates of good standing for all intermediate holding companies, tax residence certificates, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the chain structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for minimum statutory capital or subsequent capital injections exceeding €10,000
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the contributing shareholder, evidence of salary/bonus accumulation or dividend receipts, signed declaration of source of wealth, audited financial statements if the contributor is a company, copy of underlying commercial contracts, and proof that no cash or bearer instrument was used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction link of a director, shareholder, or ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport and proof of residence, tax identification number, professional reference letters, CV showing legitimate business engagement, detailed purpose-of-business letter describing the inspection agency's client countries, and evidence of no adverse sanctions or criminal records in a background check.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained payment flows expected from multiple foreign client countries (non-EU/emerging markets)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed framework agreements with each foreign client, detailed commercial invoices referencing the underlying inspection/testing order, harmonised customs/ISIC code declaration, end-client due diligence file, and a projected treasury flow forecast broken down by country and invoice reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Round-trip or immediate onward transfer of funds after receipt, particularly to entities not invoicing the SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited intercompany agreements, sub-contracting agreements with third-party inspection laboratories, a documented procurement policy, and an anti-money laundering officer's narrative confirming that all disbursements match actual trade invoices and are made to bank accounts in the name of the invoicing counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders shall be executed exclusively via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA EURO1/TARGET2 where euro-denominated, using the following standardised bank transfer protocol: (i) the remitter field must show the legal name and registered address of the contributing shareholder; (ii) the beneficiary field must show the exact registered name of the LU SARL and its IBAN; (iii) the payment purpose code must be a clear capital participation statement such as 'Capital Injection', 'Statutory Contribution', or 'Increase of Share Capital' — Luxembourg law does not require a customs form but banks will code the transaction under EU Balance of Payments (BoP) statistics; (iv) the reference field must include the corporate registration number (RCS) of the SARL; (v) the bank statement and incoming SWIFT message must be retained as the audit trail for the share capital increase or capital reduction filing at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL). For non-euro capital injections, the remitter must use a fully covered correspondent banking route, and the receiving Luxembourg bank will convert the currency at its standard spot rate, subject to no exchange control approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for factory inspection operations, third-party laboratory testing, and quality-audit subcontractors shall use the following clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for all non-urgent and urgent low-value payments, with a rigorous beneficiary bank verification step and IBAN/name-match screening; (ii) TARGET2 and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eurozone suppliers to achieve real-time finality; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (ICC UCP 600) only for high-value procurements where guarantees of payment against inspection certificates and shipping documents are required; (iv) documentary collection (UCP/URC 522) as a lower-cost alternative for established supplier relationships. All outbound payments must be matched against a validated trade invoice, purchase order, and service completion certificate from the inspection agency's internal quality-control ledger, and routed through the operational account at the tier-1 Luxembourg bank to maintain a clean audit trail suitable for Luxembourg statutory audit and tax authorities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla over-the-counter EUR/USD forward contracts with a licensed credit institution or authorised investment firm
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter EUR/CNY deliverable forwards with a permitted counterparty in Luxembourg, subject to CNY clearing availability
Cross-currency swaps for EUR/USD and EUR/GBP where the SARL has material long-term invoice flows
NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) for emerging-market currencies that are not freely deliverable, including INR, IDR, VND, and BRL, with a CSSF-licensed bank as counterparty
Exchange-traded currency futures for EUR/USD where exchange-traded margins are more capital-efficient

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting: approval of annual accounts, allocation of results, and discharge of directors/managers (décharge)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate organ; minutes and attendance records retained at the registered office and available for inspection by shareholders and competent authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; an extension may be granted by the commercial court upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual meeting within the legal deadline entitles shareholders to apply to the commercial court for judicial convocation; directors or managers lose the benefit of a timely discharge and remain exposed to liability claims; persistent default may be used as evidence of corporate irregularity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts: balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, and notes filed with the RCS and published in the RESA electronic gazette
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the annual general meeting and no later than seven months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, the outer filing date is 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is recorded as a default by the RCS; the public prosecutor may petition the commercial court to compel filing under a coercive fine; continuing default may lead to administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution; directors or managers may be held personally liable for third-party harm caused by the omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner (UBO) information in the central RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated as part of the RCS electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary of the entity's initial RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership must be declared within one month of the change irrespective of the annual anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, late filing, incomplete filing, or false confirmation may expose the SARL and its directors/managers to administrative and criminal fines up to EUR 25,000; distributions and profit-sharing may be suspended until compliant status is restored; repeated non-compliance can trigger RCS strike-off procedures and directorial disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual register review and continued maintenance of statutory corporate registers: share register, directors/managers register, minute book, and share transfer records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office of the SARL; registers are subject to inspection by shareholders, notaries, RCS officials, and tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation: each register must be updated at the time of the relevant event; a full formal annual completeness review is recommended prior to the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete, incorrect, or unavailable statutory registers may lead to fines under Luxembourg company law, loss of evidentiary weight in judicial proceedings, and personal liability of directors or managers for inaccurate member or transfer records.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) if it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average number of employees 50. Mandatory audit also applies where required by the articles of association, a supervisory authority, or applicable sectoral legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the amended law of 19 December 2002 on the accounting and annual accounts of undertakings, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is applied for consolidated accounts where required and is otherwise used only where permitted under Luxembourg law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At least once each year, within one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration date, the SARL must access the RBE online portal and confirm that all beneficial owner fields remain complete and accurate. If any share transfer, control change, or beneficial ownership change has occurred, the SARL must file an amended declaration within one month of the event. The confirmation must be submitted by an authorised director, manager, or registered fiduciary, and supporting documentation such as share transfer deeds, shareholder identification, and organisational charts must be retained in the corporate records. The UBO annual confirmation is separate from the annual accounts filing and from the annual general meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register including ownership and transfers)
Register of Directors/Managers (gérants) with appointment and termination details
Minute Book (ordinary and extraordinary shareholders' meetings and management resolutions)
Register of share transfers and supporting ownership documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 - USD 3,000 per year for professional registered office and domiciliation services; USD 1,800 - USD 4,500 per year when bundled with corporate secretarial administration, UBO confirmation, and RCS filing assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 - USD 12,500 for the statutory audit of a small or medium SARL; first-year, consolidated-reporting-related, or otherwise enlarged engagements may range up to USD 18,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg applies a combined headline CIT rate of 24.94% (17% CIT, 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax in Luxembourg City). Qualified small and medium enterprises may access an 80% exemption for qualifying intellectual property income under the IP regime, participation exemption for dividends and capital gains, and investment tax credits for digital and environmental investments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 460 - Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et l'impôt commercial, filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu Fiscaldoor e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 30 November of the calendar year following the fiscal year end for fiscal years ending 31 December; extended deadlines may apply upon justified request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCS number, legal form, registered office, tax office, director identification, and any fiscal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the SARL's full registration data; non-resident directors must attach a power of attorney and, where applicable, a Luxembourg tax representative mandate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the taxable financial year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg permanent establishment of a non-resident company, align the PE accounting data with the foreign entity's fiscal year only if formally accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss after adjustments, exemptions, and loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Luxembourg-situs taxable income attributable to the PE; all intercompany invoices must be supported by arm's-length TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying intellectual property income deduction (80%) and participation exemption for dividends/capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the nexus-ratio calculation for IP income and valid ownership evidence; non-resident shareholders claiming treaty benefits must enclose a tax residence certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, and CIT instalments paid during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit certified foreign tax credit claims; provide proof of prepayment wire transfers, including SWIFT references.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and solidarity surcharge, after credits and prepayments, plus final balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the final balance by direct debit or wire transfer to the Luxembourg treasury; retain the payment confirmation for audit purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine of EUR 25 to EUR 2,500, ex officio tax assessment, and a monthly late-payment interest charge of 0.6% of the outstanding tax. Continued default may result in enforced recovery through garnishment and asset seizure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholders must file a Luxembourg withholding tax refund or exemption claim using the official form available from the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes), attaching a valid tax residence certificate, evidence of beneficial ownership, and any applicable DTA/MLI protective declaration. Exemption at source may be obtained through the Luxembourg e-Tax system where all treaty conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on outbound statutory royalties or debt interest under domestic law. Treaty rates are therefore typically irrelevant, but payments to related parties in low-tax jurisdictions that are excessive or not at arm's length may be recharacterized as hidden profit distributions and expose the payor to a 15% dividend withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 0 (no statutory de minimis threshold); local file and master file documentation must be produced on tax audit request. Multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more are subject to country-by-country reporting and must maintain a master file as per Luxembourg CbCR law.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a formal ESR code, but the domestic anti-abuse rule under Article 56bis LIR, coupled with ATAD implementation, requires real economic substance. A SARL engaged in inspection, testing and quality control must demonstrate own premises, employees, management capability and commercial risk-taking in Luxembourg; letterbox arrangements will be disregarded and profits reattributed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable revenue from factory pre-shipment inspection and testing contracts, or fabricating expense invoices to reduce CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of board signatories up to 5 years; automatic reassessment plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, civil restitution, travel bans during enforcement proceedings, and potential imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL as a letterbox entity with no employees, physical office, or real management decision-making in Luxembourg, while booking inspection/QC fees in other jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the scheme under Article 56bis LIR, denial of DTA and participation exemption, retroactive assessment of CIT, and 15% withholding tax on deemed dividend distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto directors are personally liable for the additional tax, interest, and penalties; judicial dissolution of the entity may also be ordered by Luxembourg courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file the ultimate beneficial owner of the SARL with the Luxembourg business registry, or ignoring suspicious cross-border wire transfers and Wise payments from clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative and criminal penalties up to EUR 5 million for legal entities; prison terms up to 5 years and seizure of assets for responsible individuals under Luxembourg AML legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, compensation orders for damages, travel bans, and suspension from corporate management functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees or service charges to related corporate groups without any comparable benchmarking or retaining no TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment of taxable income, interest on the additional tax, and administrative fines of up to 10% of the reassessed tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly prepared false TP reporting are personally liable for penalty amounts and may be prosecuted for complicity in tax fraud, resulting in civil restitution and imprisonment.
